image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a metallic automotive disk brake rotor. The image focuses on the central hub area and the inner portion of the friction surface. Visible features include three lug bolt holes arranged in a triangular pattern around a large central mounting aperture. The metal surface is shiny with strong specular highlights, showing signs of machining marks and slight wear/discoloration near the center. The outer edge of the rotor and the caliper assembly are not visible in this cropped frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly a flat, circular metallic disc. Although the full diameter is cropped, the curvature and perspective confirm it is a thin disc relative to its width.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is tightly cropped on the rotor hub; the caliper, which mounts on the outer edge, is completely outside the field of view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Three distinct bolt holes are clearly visible surrounding the central aperture, consistent with a lug bolt pattern for wheel attachment.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Looking at the cutout section near the center and the side profile visible at the bottom right, there appears to be a gap between two surfaces, suggesting a ventilated design, though the fins themselves are not sharply resolved. It is definitely a structural rotor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Brake pads are housed within the caliper, which is not visible in this image.
Hydraulic lines connect to the caliper, which is out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface exhibits fine concentric striations consistent with machining lathe marks. There are no cross-drilled holes visible, but the grooves/machining marks are present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is visible brownish/yellowish discoloration and staining on the metal surface, particularly around the central hub and between the bolt holes, indicative of heat and use.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The inner edge of the large central hole appears slightly soft and lacks the sharp, machined definition expected of cast/machined metal. It blends slightly into the background void.
The three visible bolt holes do not appear perfectly equidistant or symmetrical relative to the center, which could be due to camera angle or slight AI geometric inconsistency in the hub casting.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific mechanical nature of the object and distinguish it from generic metallic discs or flywheels.
To verify the 3D structure of the ventilated rotor and ensure the central hole has proper depth rather than being a flat texture.
To check for clean edges on the cutouts and ensure no melting or fusion artifacts at the boundaries of the holes.

focus_areas: Symmetry and spacing of lug bolt holes
Depth consistency of the central aperture
Realism of metal reflections and specular highlights
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the symmetry of the bolt holes. In AI-generated mechanical parts, irregular spacing is a common failure mode. Also, verify if the 'machining marks' look like natural lathe lines or repetitive noise patterns.
